rationale: One master, cloned faithfully — the v2 learned player. The v1 clone (MIMIC) averaged eleven contradictory doctrines and its regression aim head blurred multimodal targets into a 38°-mean-error smear; the disciple studies only cuadrilla, the champion's tape (1,600,000 rows from 34 runs, stride 2), and treats aim as a 24-bin direction CLASSIFICATION (softmax + cross-entropy) so enemy-left and enemy-right stay separate choices instead of averaging to 'forward'. A 25→96→96→31 MLP. Validation on 80k held-out rows: aim top-1 bin 56.8%, top-3 82.8%, effective bin-center cosine 0.760; buttons left/right 78.7/78.6%, fire 88.5%, down 90.2%, jetpack 78.0%, reload 97.2%. Runtime interpolates the winning bin toward its stronger neighbor for sub-15° precision. Card tweak FIRE_THRESH 0.25: the master fires in disciplined windows (12% base rate), so at 0.5 the clone underfires its own good aim — probes vs the committed v1 showed 0.25 converts the 2x hit-rate edge into a 36-9 sweep (0.5 only drew). No hand-written tactics — the only rules are roam-when-alone and reload-when-empty. This card is a measurement of how much of the master survives distillation, not a title claim: the student does not expect to beat the master, but it must crush the average of eleven.
